title: Linear Regression Models
videoTitle: AP Statistics Topic 5.3 Linear Regression Models
intro: Use a linear model to predict responses, distinguish predictions from observations, and recognize extrapolation.

moments.title: When a line is appropriate
moments.text: Fit a linear model to an approximately linear association.

moments.title: Slope and intercept
moments.text: The equation gives a predicted response for any chosen x.

moments.title: Predicted response
moments.text: Use y-hat to distinguish a model prediction from an observed response.

moments.title: Model coefficients
moments.text: Technology can calculate fitted coefficients from paired data.

moments.title: Prediction direction
moments.text: A regression of y on x is designed to predict y from x.

moments.title: Salary prediction
moments.text: Substitute years of experience into the model.

moments.title: Study-time prediction
moments.text: Keep response units in the final prediction.

moments.title: Extrapolation
moments.text: Predictions beyond the observed x range can be unreliable.

cards.name: Model notation
cards.text: $\hat y=a+bx$ predicts the response from x.

cards.name: Input and output
cards.text: Substitute an explanatory value and report the predicted response with units.

cards.name: Direction matters
cards.text: A regression of y on x cannot generally be inverted to give the regression prediction of x from y.

cards.name: Prediction range
cards.text: Prefer predictions within the observed explanatory range and do not treat a fitted value as a guaranteed outcome.

questions.q: The video gives $\hat y=29059+2601.25x$, where x is years of experience and the numerical salary predictions are in dollars. Predict salary at nine years.

work.text: Use nine years for x, not for the predicted response.
The result is a fitted salary, not a promise about any employee.

questions.answer: The model predicts an annual salary of 52,470.25 dollars at nine years of experience.

questions.q: The video gives $\hat y=49.52+3.98x$, with study time x in hours and predicted exam score in points. Predict the score at 6.2 hours.

steps.t: State what the fitted response means.

work.text: Use predicted exam score and points in the answer.

questions.answer: The model predicts 74.196 exam points for a student who studies 6.2 hours.

traps.title: Prediction versus observation
traps.better: The fitted response is a prediction; actual scores vary around the model.

traps.title: Reversing the regression
traps.weak: Solve the equation for x to get the regression prediction of x.
traps.better: Predicting x from y generally requires fitting a different regression with their roles reversed.

traps.title: Extrapolation
traps.weak: A line is reliable for any input.
traps.better: The relationship may change beyond the x range used to fit the model.

traps.title: Wrong substitution
traps.weak: Put the response value into x.
traps.better: x is the explanatory input; the equation produces a predicted response.

notes.label: Wording check.
notes.text: The salary narration mentions a thousands-of-dollars axis but uses dollar-scale coefficients and predictions. The worked question explicitly uses dollars consistently.

questions.stem: A model is $\hat y=12+3x$. What is the prediction at x=4?
why: This adds the slope only once.
This adds x rather than multiplying it by the slope.

questions.stem: A model built from observations with x from 10 to 30 is used at x=80. This is:
why: A residual compares actual and predicted responses.
A single fitted value is not an interval.

questions.stem: Which notation identifies a fitted response?
why: y usually denotes an observed response.
The hat identifies a model prediction.

questions.stem: Why is solving a fitted y-on-x equation for x not generally an x-on-y regression prediction?
opts: The two fits minimize different response residuals
Correlation changes sign when variables are swapped
Every line has the same slope
why: The issue is statistical purpose, not algebraic ability.
The regression fitting criterion depends on which variable is the response.
Slopes depend on the fitted relation and units.

sections.title: Write a complete response
sections.prompt: A model for bicycle repair cost is $\hat y=18+12x$, where x is repair time in hours and y is cost in dollars. It was fitted using jobs lasting 0.5–4 hours.
parts: (a) Predict the cost of a 2.5-hour job.
(b) Interpret the prediction and explain why it is not an observed bill.
(c) Assess using this model for a 12-hour job or to predict repair time from a known bill.
sample: (b) For a repair lasting 2.5 hours, the model predicts a cost of 48 dollars. The actual bill may differ; the equation supplies a fitted response, not the recorded charge.

(c) A 12-hour job is outside the fitted range and requires extrapolation, which may be unreliable. Predicting time from a bill requires a regression designed for that direction; simply inverting this fitted equation is not generally equivalent.
checklist: Describes a predicted, not guaranteed, cost.
Explains the direction of regression prediction.
